author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Britain’s domestic intelligence chief is warning that the next major security shock could be developing outside the areas receiving the most attention, arguing that agencies should avoid preparing only for the last crisis.

MI5 Director General Ken McCallum made the case in an opinion article marking 25 years since the September 11 attacks. He said al Qaeda has been diminished but remains a threat, while governments must also contend with state-backed sabotage and cyberattacks capable of disrupting essential infrastructure such as power systems.

The warning did not identify a specific imminent plot. Instead, it framed the central challenge as anticipating changing methods and actors while maintaining defenses against known terrorist networks.

McCallum called for closer work among government, private companies and academic specialists. That coordination has become more important as critical services rely on interconnected technology and as hostile activity can move between physical operations, online systems and influence campaigns. His remarks add to an ongoing debate over how security resources should be divided between counterterrorism and broader state-linked threats.
dek: Ken McCallum says security agencies must not prepare only for familiar threats as terrorism, sabotage and cyber risks continue to evolve.
headline: MI5 chief warns next strategic shock may emerge beyond current focus
